Comments: On 12/16/2024, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the HAMBLETON WELL PAD in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County. During 09/17/2024 inspection (SAIR 3832442) the 5H GPU was leaking over range fluid. No violations were issued. The following was observed during inspection:- 5H GPU appeared repaired and GPU parts replaced (Photo 1).-It appears multiple production tanks and secondary containment was removed. I observed one production tank within new secondary containment (Photo 2). Production tank spill containment appears to be overflowing. No elevated readings. I recommend removing fluid (Photo 3 and 4).-I observed elevated conductivity readings within a 90 x 90 ft section where production tanks and secondary containment appeared removed. Multiple elevated readings were found 4-7 inches below the surface. The department requests clarification as to when and why the production tanks were removed. The Field Scout Conductivity probe was calibrated on 12/16/24 before inspection was conducted. The operator was contacted and notified on 12/16/24. The following violations are being issued for: 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.34(a), 91.33(a),

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. Conditions at the site at the time of inspection indicate that this estimate is reasonable. The released production fluid was under pressure and escaped as a mist. The area of the spill appears to be contained near the well equipment, but stressed vegetation could be found up to 65 feet from the wellhead. Because the estimated spill volume is greater than 1 bbl, an Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process should be followed.

Violation ID: 8206967
Permit API: 027-21225
Unconventional: No
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/05/2024
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 027-21225 with Justin Galiolto of DEP and the property owners on November 5, 2024. During the inspection two leaks were identified. A brine leak was observed coming from an open annulus vent on the bottom of the well head (photos 1-3). A hole approximately 2'x2' was observed at the drip. Large rocks were placed in this hole. I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe and got a blinking reading of 4.0 mS/cm. The soil probe max's out at 4.0 mS/cm.The second leak was observed coming from where the brine pipe attaches to the brine tank near of the top of the 50 BBL tank (pictures 4-5). A wet black streak was observed running down the side of the brine tank was well. Please note that the brine tank was full of fluids. A 5X Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were observed. I contacted Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC at ~1230 and made her aware of my findings. At ~1300 Ms. Empfield notified me to let me know Diversified personal were enroute to go investigate the brine leaks. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown quantity of brine released and unknown amount of time the leaks have been occurring, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 for site remediation.

I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe and got a blinking reading of 4.0 mS/cm. The soil probe max's out at 4.0 mS/cm.The second leak was observed coming from where the brine pipe attaches to the brine tank near of the top of the 50 BBL tank (pictures 4-5). A wet black streak was observed running down the side of the brine tank was well. Please note that the brine tank was full of fluids. A 5X Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were observed. I contacted Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC at ~1230 and made her aware of my findings. At ~1300 Ms. Empfield notified me to let me know Diversified personal were enroute to go investigate the brine leaks. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown quantity of brine released and unknown amount of time the leaks have been occurring, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 for site remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/13/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8187540
Permit API: 003-22657
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Fawn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/13/2024
Comments: On May 13, 2024 the Department conducted an incident inspection in regards to a spill that occurred at the Sun Mine Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued on 9/11/2023 and expires on 9/10/2028) on May 10, 2024. According to Derek Zofchak of Range Resources, the spill occurred at 12 PM when drill cuttings and soap slurry fluid entered the flare stack eco tank (which normally separates fluids from gas), the float on the pump within the eco tank malfunctioned and as a result, fluid (approximately 30 gallons of drill cuttings and soap slurry) that normally would not get carried over to the flare stack ended up spewing out of the flare stack as a fine mist onto the graveled well pad and well pad fill slope. At the time of the inspection, Range Resources notified the Department that the spill had been remediated. Two roll off dumpsters were on site filled with waste material, the well pad appeared to be scraped on the left hand side of the flare stack, and new seed and mulch was seen on the the fill slope and berm directly in front of and to the left-hand side of the flare stack. Soil conductivity readings were taken to determine if any areas were still contaminated, a background was done on the far back side of the well site perimeter upslope (0.03 mS) then readings were taken outside of the approximate release area to the far left of the flare stack on the pad (0.0085 mS and 0.016 mS), then moving forward into the approximate release area (0.0146 mS), another was taken fairly close to the flare stack on the left-hand side in a wet looking spot in the gravel (0.327 mS), directly next to the flare stack in a wet-looking section of gravel (0.293 mS). Then a reading was taken from the right side of the flare stack where Range claims was not impacted and therefore was not scrapped (0.088 mS). A reading was taken directly behind the flare stack right at the base of the berm before the fill slope (0.138 mS), in the berm directly behind the flare stack (0.081 mS), outside of the area that Range replaced on the fill slope where they say was not impacted (0.130 mS), and lastly three were taken from the area of the fill slope that was replaced (0.100 mS, 0.131 mS and 0.209 mS). Based on the soil conductivity readings, it appears that all contaminated material that was present on the fill slope, berm and the well pad to the left/in front of the flare stack has been removed. Range stated that the flare stack eco pump was taken apart for examination and nothing was found to be wrong with it. According to Range this was just a random malfunction and they do not anticipate that it will occur again. The Department recommends Range place the flare stack inside secondary containment in case this were to occur again.Based on todays inspection the Department concludes this release has been immediately corrected in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/09/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Keating Twp, McKean county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/09/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 964823
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Swepi Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-11
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 843949
Permit API: 117-21454
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Shippen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-03-11
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection at the SWEPI LP - Houck 433 well pad located in Shippen Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/11/2019 @1130 hours. Matt Skolny, SWEPI LP was present on the pony pad for the spill investigation. Morgan Davis, SWEPI LP OSR was present on the main pad. The weather was 37 degrees, sunny, winds WNW 15mph, the previously deposited snow is melting causing the site to the very muddy with standing water. April Heater, SWEPI LP reported a spill to the DEP's regional office on 3/8/2019 @1500 hours. Onsite personnel were breaking apart the "fastline", which was used to carry frack fluid from the AST on the pony pad to the main pad. Mr. Skolny stated they had run a number of courses of freshwater through the line to clean it out. When the line was dismantled the open end was placed in a tub, on secondary containment, on the NW corner of the pony pad. No fluid came out initially, but when the onsite personnel left to work on another area, fluid was discharged from the end of the pipe. The fluid overtopped containment, and entered the channel in the NW corner of the pad. SWEPI estimated `20 gallons of fluid was released into containent with `20 gallons overtopping and discharging into the perimeter E&S ditch. As of today's inspection, a tub of icy, black, frozen/slush mix that was initially recovered from the channel had a field measured conductivity of 3.0 mS/cm. This tub was placed on secondary containment for disposal. The channel off the edge of the pad was full of ice/snow with a small volume of liquid. No elevated conductivity was measured in the ditch or in puddles on the corner of the pony pad. A black greasy material and oily sheen was observed in the NW corner of the ditch. SWEPI was notified and instructed to have the material removed from the ditch. Matt Bailey was present onsite at this point, and stated he would have the remaining issues addressed. Due to the reported release of fluids onto the ground surface, violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a56(a) Temporary Storage SWMA 301 Solid Waste Management Act CSL 402(b) Potential Pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth An inspection of the main pad was also conducted. The coil rig was observed drilling out plugs on the 6H well on the main pad. Mr. Davis, SWEPI OSR accompanied me around the well pad during the inspection. A few areas of elevated conductivity were discovered inside containment. Mr. Davis stated he would have the fluid removed when the vac truck returned to the site. Mr. Davis was also notified of containment berms that appeared broken/smashed and were in need of repair. Although the site was very muddy, with large amounts of standing water, none of the puddles on the pad surface were found to have elevated conductivity. The E&S trap and rock-lined channels appeared frozen. No sedimentation or erosion was observed. I departed the site at 1345 hours.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of South Enterline Road in July 1997. This site should be remediated as a visual cleanup.

Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 2019-11-13
Comments: On 11/13/19 a follow up inspection of the site was conducted in response to violations noted on 7/14/16 and in preparation for a meeting with the operator. The following was observed: >>The initial inspection on 7/14/16 found: "A large erosion channel leading off of the access road and into the surrounding brush was found near coordinates N40°11'03.29” W80°01'01.32”. This constitutes violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion." >>An inspection on 8/15/19 found: "The erosion channel described in the prior inspection was remediated and in good condition. A second channel extended along the middle half of the access road on the uphill side. This constitutes violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion." >>At the time of inspection barren and possibly eroded soils were found near around the outlet of the under road culvert at the location of the initial erosion channel near the bottom of the access road. Additional erosion channels were noted forming along much of the improved access road with some extending away from the access road into the surrounding brush. These continue to constitute violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion. Increased monitoring and remediation possibly including rock check dams are encouraged. A meeting is scheduled for 11/14/19 with the operator to discuss ongoing conditions and remediations options at this and other nearby sites.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/16/2021 to GEOPETRO LLC in Mercer Twp, Butler county. OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GEOPETRO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/16/2021
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 926912
Permit API: 019-21988
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Mercer Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/16/2021
Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all four wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21988, along with three other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21992, 019-21993, 019-22002), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the act nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2762573 and 2762664, (conducted in early August 2018), suggest that only well number 019-22002 was ever stimulated. Additionally, it was indicated that, at the time, RE Gas intended to plug all four wells beginning with the three that had not been stimulated. The wells were never plugged. An inspection dated 07/26/2018 (ID#:2769196) cites violations for failure to restore the well location, 78a65(a)1i and OGA3216(A). ESCGP number ESX12-019-0148 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 07/17/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4106458 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation that was issued in issued in IR 4084771 was left outstanding in IR 4106458, for failure to have a written restoration plan narrative onsite. The remaining violations issued in IR 4084771 were not left outstanding in IR 4106458, as they could not be evaluated due to the snow cover during the time of IR 4106458. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4084771 from the operator by December 4, 2025. However, no formal response to IR 4084771 has been received to-date from the operator.The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign has been removed from the entrance of the pre-existing access road (photo 1). The access road is to remain unrestored, as it predates construction of the well site (photos 2-4). Temporary stabilization is inconsistent throughout the former well site, as large areas of exposed soil were observed on the slopes at the northern and southern site boundaries (photos 7, 8, 15, and 16). No loose sediment was observed in the rock-lined channels that empty into the pre-existing Sediment Trap (photos 9 and 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed at the northern and southern boundaries (photos 9, 11, 17, and 19). The improperly installed super silt fence which was identified in IR 4084771 remains, with the fabric having completely detached and fallen to the ground (photo 18). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator reassess whether the E and S controls installed on site are adequate for this well site restoration.The Department also continues to recommend that the operator apply additional temporary stabilization where bare soil is exposed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4084771 shall remain outstanding. An additional violation shall be issued against the lack of adequate temporary stabilization at the northern and southern site boundaries.

Violation ID: 873436
Permit API: 015-23413
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: On January 10, 2020, Department representative John Ciccone conducted an investigation in response to a reported spill at Chief's SGL-36 pad. Kellon Balum (Chief Oil & Gas) notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins) that on January 9, 2020 at 0900 hours, of a spill of approximately 1-2 barrels of a production fluid/freshwater mixture to soil at the SGL-36 Pad in Overton Township, Bradford County. The department arrived onsite at 1000 hours and met with Kellon Balum and Brendan Logan of Chief Oil and Gas. The site was busy with tankers driving onto / off of the pad. During a pressure test, a 2 inch hole was discovered in a saddle unit. Before the hole could be fixed, a check valve failed which resulted in the spill of a mixture of production fluids and freshwater. Since the incident has been reported, the gate valve and check valve have been replaced in order to ensure subsequent failures do not happen. The site of the spill (photo #1) has been excavated by contractor Thompson. The excavation was being overseen by Brendan Logan of Chief. The excavated pit was dug out down to bedrock. No standing water was noted within the pit during the time of the inspection. Dug out soil was placed within 2 waste management (WM) containers (photo #2). 1 WM container will be shipped out to Waste Management today, and the other will remain onsite within its secondary containment for possible future use. Chief was in process of extending the excavated pit in order to ensure thorough removal of impacted soils during the time of the inspection. Site was departed at 1040 hours. The release of production fluids on the well pad is in violation of CSL 402(b), 78a.57, and SWMA 301. This release has been referred to Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields due to the quantity reported. Violations cited.

Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-12-20
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the Burchianti 11A gas well and production equipment on 12/20/2019. Diversified personnel are on location at the time of the inspection. The Department was notified by PEMA on 12/20/2019 of a loud explosion associated with the Burchianti 11A gas well. At the time of the inspection, the Burchianti 11A gas well is shut in. The operator shut in the well at approximately 2330 on 12/19/2019 in response to a production equipment failure. According to the operator, a failure of the production equipment caused explosive damage to the production equipment and a release of gas from the well. The gas release occurred from 2210 - 2330 on 12/19/2019 until the well was shut in by the operator at 2330 on 12/19/2109. The well is located approximately 300 feet north the production equipment and production tanks. No damage to the well was observed. At the location of the production equipment the Department observed damaged pieces of production equipment. The Department observed some gray black stained gravel at the former location of the separator. The gravel appears to be damp. Damage to the production unit is severe. Diversified personnel are searching the wooded area around the well site for additional pieces of the production equipment. The Department observed pieces of equipment being recovered approximately 70 feet from the source of the failure. Search and recovery of damaged equipment continued while the Department was on site. Two production tanks are located within an earthen containment adjacent to the location of the explosion. The Department observed small holes in the south side of the southern most tank. The north tank in the containment is severely corroded. A large severely corroded hole was observed on the southwest side upper portion of the tank. The hole is approximately 3' x 5'. The Department did not detect any combustible levels of gas during the inspection. In response to the incident, Diversified reported that surrounding wells have been shut in.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO

Violation Date: 2/04/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8263956
Permit API: 129-29235
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/04/2026
Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2022 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Jones Twp, Elk county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 959586
Permit API: 047-25102
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2022
Comments: This inspection is being performed in response to a report of a previous spill that occurred in February. It was reported that a containment overflow allowed production water to leak and eventually run down the access road and into a vegetated area, and was not reported to DEP. It appears as though the leak source is from a valve cluster sitting along the Billy Buck Rd. Some production water leaked and was cleaned up Feb 3. However, some of the product was not collected at the time and ran down the ditch/access road approximately 150 feet before crossing the access road and running into the pipeline corridor on the south side of Billy Buck Rd. The water appears to have spread across the corridor in multiple fingers, causing a kill zone in each location. Elevated conductivity readings >20 mS were noted on the pipeline corridor. The operator was contacted regarding these findings, and further investigation will be done to determine the scope and impact of the spill.

Comments: At 11:20 pm I observed two mobile storage tanks, one green and one red, approximately 400 feet to the east of well 318. The green tank had fluid actively running from an unsecured valve at the bottom of the tank. Conductivity readings taken from the fluid were 7280 micro S. A large puddle could be seen between the two tanks and under them. A conductivity reading from the puddle was 5270 micro S. The fluid from inside the tank is brine. The Department contacted the operator and Mr. Ty Catalone, Vac truck driver was dispatched to the site. He clamped a hose onto the valve stopping the leak. He climbed on top of the tank and stated that it was nearly empty, but he would suck it out. His actions stopped the discharge of brine from the tank.

CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8275346
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Comments: On 10/15/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 49 degrees and overcast when I arrived on site. Rainfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Prior to this inspection, Seneca personnel had told me that a construction crew was being mobilized to the site to restore the pad back to well pad condition, repairing the spots that were excavated after the release discovered on 5/13/2025. When I arrived on site I did witness some construction equipment at the site. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. A Gas Field Specialist crew was on site digging an 8-foot-deep trench across the pad north of the well cellars. Short, downward sloping trenches from each well cellar would be installed to the long trench and then layered with gravel. Clean out pipes will be installed on the east and west end of the long trench with another one in the center. Liquids coming from the well cellars could be monitored in this trench and collected if necessary. A different construction company will be repairing the rest of the pad.Field conductivity readings taken during this inspection are as follows: Liquid on the northeast corner of the pad being 1.066 mS conductance or less. Liquid below the west disturbed area on the fill slope being 0.769 mS conductance. Liquid flowing down from the east fill slope disturbed area being 1.212 mS conductance. Liquid in the sump pit at the northwest corner of the location being 1.315 mS conductance. This fluid was being pumped up to the pad surface into a frac tank on the pad. Soil probe readings taken below the rock lined swale on the west side of the pad being 0.501 mS conductance or less.There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well has not been successfully plugged yet. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated areas.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1000 hours.

Comments: Onsite for a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3602052 dated 8/17/2023. The previous inspection report references a black plastic brine line, (2) brine tanks, and a separate tank battery with (4) steel tanks.There is a 100bbl fiberglass tank and a 100bbl poly tank onsite that appears to be the brine storage tanks for the well. The two tanks are plumbed together with piping and valves open to equalize the fluid in each tank. There does not appear to be a way to empty either tank by means of a water truck hose connection without altering the plumbing of the tanks. However, the 2" black poly line that runs from the hillside from the wells on the lease and ties into the brine tanks has a "T" fitting and a valve to discharge produced fluid to the ground via a ditch from a cross-culvert of the access road.The 2" valve on the black poly pipeline is closed and plugged. The pipe was not actively discharging or leaking. However, there is a visible impact area within the ditch of the cross-culvert and which the black poly line is laid. Soil conductivity readings indicate that a brine discharge has occurred at the site. The impacted area inside the ditch extends approximately 80' downslope from the access road culvert and ending just before a second culvert for another old access road. The width on average of the ditch is about 5'. The amount of the discharged produced fluid is unknown.Violations are cited.

Impaired water was discharged off containment to the well pad. The impaired water traveled a collection ditch and left the well pad and was discharged on the well pad slope.
